Shares of IBM (IBM) currently trade at 19.9 times earnings, while the S&P 500 sits at 21.9. Investors buying at that multiple need to understand the underlying assets, and the company has recently changed its messaging. During the fiscal Q2 2025 call, executives focused on a running total of generative AI business that they defined as their book of business. The most recent presentation offered a different focal point. So what is management talking up instead?

IBM Now Talks Up Recurring Software Revenue

Executives are now framing the company around reliable, repeating software revenue. During the fiscal Q2 2026 call on July 22, 2026, the company noted that about 80% of its annual software revenue is recurring. This division accounts for nearly 45% of total revenue.

A year prior, leadership anchored its pitch to a different metric. During the fiscal Q2 2025 call, the company reported its generative AI book of business stood at over $7.5 billion since inception. That figure climbed from over $3 billion during the fiscal Q3 2024 call. Highlighting a rapidly growing cumulative total gave investors a straightforward view into AI demand.

Generative AI remains part of the conversation. Management noted on the latest call that the technology represented about 50% of quarterly Consulting signings. Yet the company has stopped emphasizing the cumulative tally.

Software Is IBM's Largest Source Of Revenue

The software unit brought in $30.0 billion in fiscal 2025, accounting for 44% of the company's revenue over that period. Sales in the division expanded by 10.6%, compared with a 1.8% growth rate for Consulting, which is the second-largest business segment.

The company also tracks annual recurring revenue. Executives placed that metric at $24.6 billion during the most recent call, representing an 8% increase from a year earlier.

The generative AI metric measured a different type of performance: a cumulative book of business since inception. It never reflected actual yearly sales, whereas recurring software revenue provides an annual baseline.

Is IBM's Turn To Software Good News For You?

This strategic pivot toward software presents a more reassuring than concerning picture for investors, though it comes with a catch. A baseline of repeating revenue offers more stability than a lifetime tally of generative AI business, and this reliable income anchors the largest division at the company.

The complication is that software is also where IBM missed expectations during fiscal Q2 2026. Software revenue grew 5% for the quarter, but its organic growth was flat. Executives noted that tens of large deals failed to close on time, and that about a third of those delayed contracts had finalized by the earnings call.

title: What Is Adobe No Longer Telling You?

What Is Adobe No Longer Telling You?

Adobe (ADBE) stock is priced at 12.9 times earnings, compared to a 21.9 multiple for the S&P 500. Yet even at that valuation, investors need to understand exactly what they hold as corporate priorities shift. Just a year ago, executives highlighted how much of the company's subscription revenue was influenced by AI. They no longer emphasize that measure. So what does Adobe point to now?

Adobe Now Points To A Narrower AI Number

The software maker now spotlights revenue specifically from products sold as AI products, which it brands as AI-first. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives said that total new AI-influenced recurring revenue exceeded one-third of the business, after widening the measure to include the newer AI-first products.

This metric offers a much tighter lens than the previous standard. During the fiscal Q3 2025 call, leadership stated that recurring revenue influenced by AI had passed $5 billion. By the following quarter, executives said their strategy was to drive all recurring revenue through AI-influenced products. That broader measure served to signal that AI was already a component of what many customers were paying for.

Adobe's AI Products Are Still A Small Business

This AI-first recurring revenue accounted for more than 2% of Adobe's $27.5 billion in total recurring revenue during fiscal Q3 2026. The former metric painted a vastly larger picture. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives noted the AI-influenced figure exceeded one-third of all recurring revenue, adding that the newer AI-first products were factored into that total.

Even so, these dedicated AI products are expanding at a much sharper clip than the broader business. Executives reported that AI-first recurring revenue grew more than 150% from a year earlier, while total recurring revenue increased 11.2%. For context, during the fiscal Q1 2025 call, leadership said the AI-first lineup had contributed more than $125 million of recurring revenue.

Customer engagement with the tools is also rising. According to executives, AI usage picked up from the prior quarter across both Creative Cloud and the Firefly app.

Should Adobe Shareholders Welcome The Narrower Number?

Yes, with two caveats. The narrower metric counts only AI products that customers actually pay for, and it is growing quickly, so it is the stricter of the two measures. That provides a reassuring signal for those holding the stock.

The risk lies in the scale of those products. They remain a small fraction of the overall business, meaning the bulk of an investment in Adobe is tied to the rest of the subscription base. At the same time, the company is giving more away to acquire users. Monthly users of its free creative products passed 100 million, up more than 70% from a year earlier. Contracted future revenue grew 8% over the same period. When asked in September about posting the first single-digit growth in that metric since early fiscal 2023, executives tied the pace to their focus on signing up free users, noting the figure steps up in the fourth quarter.

What Would It Take For Salesforce Stock To Move Higher?

Salesforce (CRM) stock has lost 3.8% over the past twelve months, trailing the 17.3% return of the S&P 500. Executives say their job with artificial intelligence is to deliver new value to customers. During the fiscal Q2 2027 earnings call on August 26, 2026, management described an upgrade that most of its users have not made yet.

Salesforce Wants Its Customers On Premium Editions

Salesforce is waiting to sell its customers an upgrade. The company packages its newest AI features within premium editions of its software, and management noted that clients seeking these features must move to higher-end tiers. One such feature combines an AI model with the data a customer already stores inside Salesforce.

Few users have made the transition so far. Only 5% of the people who use Salesforce's sales and service software have upgraded to the higher-end editions, according to management. Yet the company stated that customers that have started using Salesforce's AI agents already spend about twice as much a year with the company, on average.

Agentforce's Recurring Revenue Is Small Beside The Whole Company

Agentforce, the company's product for AI agents, reached $1.5 billion of annual recurring revenue in fiscal Q2 2027. That figure remains a small fraction of the $43.9 billion of revenue Salesforce generated over the last twelve months.

The growth opportunity lies in the software those upgrades are sold into. Sales and service applications represent its two largest segments, posting $9.0 billion and $9.8 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026. Together they made up roughly 45% of the company's revenue that year, and each grew by about 8%.

Management has outlined broader ambitions for the business. In September, executives set a target of more than $63 billion in revenue for fiscal 2030. That compares with the $41.5 billion reported for fiscal 2026.

The share price appears to assume some of this growth already. The stock has risen 40% in the past three months, compared with 3.8% for the index. Still, the shares remain 11.5% below their 52-week high.

What Has Salesforce Not Yet Shown Investors?

Salesforce has not yet disclosed how much of Agentforce's revenue comes from customers who are past the trial stage. When asked about this during the August 26 call, management provided a count instead: the company added 2,000 paying customers into production, and said the number of accounts with agents in production grew 70% from the quarter before.

Users can now access Salesforce through tools like Slack without opening the company's dedicated software screens. Management said it is still determining how to charge for that access.

title: Is Snowflake Stock Riskier Than It Looks?
detail:
Is Snowflake Stock Riskier Than It Looks?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

Snowflake (SNOW) stock has returned 169% over the past six months, against 14.0% for the S&P 500. Investors appear to believe artificial intelligence has put the company on a faster growth track, and the latest quarter supports that view. Yet on the most recent earnings call, executives pointed out a catch in the AI business. So what is the catch?

What Did Snowflake's Management Flag About AI?

Executives said Snowflake earns less on its AI sales than on the rest of its product lineup. During the fiscal Q2 2027 call on September 2, 2026, the company lowered its fiscal 2027 forecast for adjusted product gross margin to 74%, from 75% on the prior call. Management cited a larger share of sales coming from fast-growing AI workloads, where the contribution margin is lower today.

AI represents a major source of that new growth. Product revenue growth accelerated to 37% year over year in fiscal Q2 2027, and executives noted that AI products contributed about half of that acceleration. Adoption is spreading quickly, as CoWork, one of Snowflake's AI products, expanded to reach 5,800 total accounts in the quarter. So the faster the AI business expands, the more of Snowflake's sales come at a thinner margin.

Snowflake Depends On Product Revenue For 95% Of Sales

Product revenue reached $4.5 billion in fiscal 2026, up 29.2% from the prior year. That segment makes up 95% of Snowflake's total revenue, and the AI workloads are sold directly inside it. The thinner margin on AI therefore sits inside Snowflake's main business, not in a side project.

Current valuations leave little room for that. Snowflake trades at 23.2 times its sales, compared with 3.1 for the S&P 500. The stock also sits just 2.3% below its high for the past year. Yet the company lost money over the past twelve months, so a price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful. The net margin was negative 20.1%, against a profit of 13.3% for the broader index.

The share price appears to assume that rapid growth will translate into profit. Management noted the company remains on track for a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2028. However, with a thinner margin on AI sales, Snowflake has less to work with on the way there.

Is Snowflake's Profit Plan Holding Up So Far?

So far, executives say the plan is intact. On the same call, management raised the fiscal 2027 forecast for adjusted operating margin to 14.5%, up from 13.5%. The company stated it is offsetting growing cloud costs with slowing headcount expense. This protects the operating margin, but it is not the same as AI sales becoming more profitable on their own.

title: Intuit vs. Oracle: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

Intuit vs. Oracle: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

ORCL
INTU
AAPL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often choose between established tech giants like Intuit (NASDAQ:INTU) and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) when seeking growth and stability. Both companies are currently navigating a rapidly changing digital landscape for enterprise software.

Intuit focuses on personal finance and small business tools like TurboTax and QuickBooks, which help users manage taxes and accounting. Oracle provides heavy-duty infrastructure and cloud applications for massive global organizations. They are being compared as top tech stocks that dominate their respective niches while expanding into advanced artificial intelligence services.

The case for Intuit

Intuit operates primarily as a global financial technology platform for consumers and small businesses. Its business model relies on a suite of tools including TurboTax and QuickBooks that manage complex financial tasks for roughly 93 million customers. The company distributes its products through major third-party platforms such as Apple and maintains commercial agreements with numerous financial institutions.

In fiscal 2026 (ending in July), revenue reached $21 billion, representing growth of roughly 14% compared to the previous year. The company reported net income of close to $4.6 billion, resulting in a net margin of approximately 21%.

As of its July 2026 balance sheet, Intuit has a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity. The current ratio is roughly 1.5x, indicating it can meet short-term debt obligations.

Free cash flow reached $8.6 billion after subtracting capital expenditures from operating cash. Note that stock-based compensation was roughly 23% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash since it is a non-cash expense.

The case for Oracle

Oracle provides enterprise software and cloud infrastructure services to a global customer base in more than 145 countries. Its key growth driver is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, which supports IT frameworks for businesses, government agencies, and educational institutions. The company manages a vast network of partners and has recently integrated substantial acquisitions to bolster its data services and content delivery.

In fiscal 2026 (ending in May), revenue reached approximately $67 billion, which reflects growth of 17% over the prior period. Net income for the year was $17 billion, resulting in a healthy net margin of nearly 25%. These results demonstrate the scale of its operations as it transitions more customers to its recurring cloud subscription model.

Microsoft plans to scale its Azure Maia chip deployments starting in 2027, with Maia 300 expected to enter production deployments that year.

Microsoft, Marvell and Oracle formed an Open Compute Project working group to develop an open specification for integrated hardware security in cloud data centers.

Earlier, Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick raised his price target to $600 from $550 while maintaining a 'Buy' rating. The move was part of the firm's first-quarter earnings preview.

Microsoft (MSFT) is drawing investor attention after Barclays raised its price target on the stock to $600 from $512 while maintaining an 'Overweight' rating.

Barclays adjusted the target as part of its third-quarter software earnings preview, and said the quarter "should start showing more differentiation in software," according to The Fly.

MSFT shares were trading 1.5% higher at the time of writing on Tuesday. Microsoft's market capitalization reached $4.02 trillion at Monday's close, surpassing the $4 trillion threshold for the first time since October 2025.

Analysts Offer Mixed Views On Microsoft

Barclays' latest note follows analyst updates from Deutsche Bank and Phillip Securities on Monday, according to The Fly.

Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick raised his price target to $600 from $550 while maintaining a 'Buy' rating. The move was part of the firm's first-quarter earnings preview.

Phillip Securities downgraded Microsoft to 'Neutral' from 'Accumulate' and set a $515 price target, citing the recent re-rating of the shares.

Microsoft Joins Marvell, Oracle In Data-Center Security Initiative

Microsoft, Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Oracle (ORCL) announced on Tuesday that they have established a working group under the Open Compute Project (OCP) to develop an open specification for an integrated hardware security module (HSM) for cloud and hyperscale data centers.

The proposed solution is designed to support secure cryptographic key caching and key lifecycle management at the server level. The companies said the approach aims to reduce latency, improve scalability and strengthen cloud workload security.

The working group plans to define an open specification incorporating a hardware security boundary, key vault and attestation chain directly into servers. The companies are targeting an initial draft for the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, with version 1.0 to follow.
